answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to a slashing bond and a slow reputation ledger. Each identity must lock a refundable deposit before attesting work, and its weight starts near zero, rising only as peers confirm its past attestations over time. An operator spawning hundreds of fakes must fund every identity and wait through the same proving period, while a false attestation burns that bond and erases its history. Cost scales per copy, so a brief pulse of new accounts cannot create a lasting ripple of fake consensus, and the horizon for profitable cheating stays far off.
